name: # Golden Crust Bakery
brief:
# Golden Crust Bakery — Marketing Website

## What this is
A marketing website for a neighbourhood bakery called Golden Crust. The site is
public, read-mostly, and exists to get a hungry visitor to walk in or place an
order. It must be fast on a phone, work without JavaScript for the core content,
and be trivially editable by the owner.

## Audience
- Local residents deciding where to buy bread and pastries today.
- People ordering a celebration cake or a catering box ahead of time.
- Tourists searching "bakery near me" on a phone.

## Required pages / sections
1. **Home** — hero with today's fresh-bake highlights, opening-hours badge that
   shows Open/Closed computed from the current time and the hours table, and a
   short story block.
2. **Menu** — grouped products (Breads, Pastries, Cakes, Drinks). Each item has a
   name, short description, price, and allergen tags (gluten, dairy, nuts, egg,
   vegan). Filter by dietary tag and by category, plus a text search box.
3. **Hours & Location** — a weekly table of opening hours, a holiday-closures
   list, an embedded static map image, and a "Get directions" link.
4. **Order form** — a celebration-cake / catering enquiry form: name, phone,
   email, pickup date, product, quantity, and free-text notes. Must validate the
   pickup date is at least 48 hours in the future, require either phone or email,
   and show a clear confirmation with an order reference.
5. **Contact** — phone, email, address, social links, and a short FAQ.

## Functional requirements
- Opening-hours logic must be a single source of truth reused by the Home badge
  and the Hours page (compute Open/Closed from the same table).
- The menu filter must combine category, dietary tag, and free-text query with
  AND semantics, and show a friendly empty state when nothing matches.
- The order form must reject a missing contact method, a pickup date under 48
  hours away, and a quantity below 1; on success it generates a human-readable
  order reference (e.g. GC-2026-0007) and echoes the full order back.
- Prices are shown in GBP with two decimals; totals for quantity > 1 are
  computed.
- All form validation errors are field-level and accessible (associated with the
  input, announced to screen readers).

## Non-functional requirements
- Responsive from 320px to 1440px; mobile-first.
- Core content (menu, hours, contact) readable with JS disabled.
- Semantic HTML landmarks, one h1 per page, alt text on every image.
- Colour contrast at least WCAG AA.
- No third-party trackers.

## Explicitly out of scope
- Online payment / card processing.
- User accounts or login.
- A real database or CMS backend — content is static data in the app.
- Multi-language support.

artifacts.title: Phase narrative (LLM)
artifacts.body:
For the Golden Crust Bakery project's P0 deep research and feasibility phase, the investigation focused on the legal and operational groundwork required before any marketing site build could meaningfully proceed—specifically, how a neighbourhood bakery would secure and formalize its physical location. Research surfaced a consistent landscape of free, template-driven lease and rental agreement resources (eForms, LawDistrict, and various landlord form libraries), all converging on the same core mechanics: a lease is a legal document granting a tenant the right to occupy space in exchange for rent, contingent on landlord verification of credit and background information, with both parties bound to fixed or periodic terms. This finding confirms that lease execution is a well-templated, low-cost step, but it also flags a feasibility dependency—the bakery's physical address, foot-traffic assumptions, and local-search positioning cannot be validated until a rental agreement is actually authorized, meaning the marketing website's audience targeting ("local residents deciding where to buy bread") remains theoretical until the storefront is legally secured. Consequently, the phase concludes that the project is feasible from a content and legal-forms standpoint, but the website's local-SEO and walk-in strategy should be treated as blocked pending confirmation of a signed lease and a verified physical location.

## Mission
# Golden Crust Bakery — Marketing Website

## What this is
A marketing website for a neighbourhood bakery called Golden Crust. The site is
public, read-mostly, and exists to get a hungry visitor to walk in or place an
order. It must be fast on a phone, work without JavaScript for the core content,
and be trivially editable by the owner.

## Audience
- Local residents deciding where to buy bread and pastries today.
- People ordering a celebration cake or a catering box ahead of time.
- Tourists searching "bakery near me" on a phone.

## Required pages / sections
1. **Home** — hero with today's fresh-bake highlights, opening-hours badge that
   shows Open/Closed computed from the current time and the hours table, and a
   short story block.
2. **Menu** — grouped products (Breads, Pastries, Cakes, Drinks). Each item has a
   name, short description, price, and allergen tags (gluten, dairy, nuts, egg,
   vegan). Filter by dietary tag and by category, plus a text search box.
3. **Hours & Location** — a weekly table of opening hours, a holiday-closures
   list, an embedded static map image, and a "Get directions" link.
4. **Order form** — a celebration-cake / catering enquiry form: name, phone,
   email, pickup date, product, quantity, and free-text notes. Must validate the
   pickup date is at least 48 hours in the future, require either phone or email,
   and show a clear confirmation with an order reference.
5. **Contact** — phone, email, address, social links, and a short FAQ.

## Functional requirements
- Opening-hours logic must be a single source of truth reused by the Home badge
  and the Hours page (compute Open/Closed from the same table).
- The menu filter must combine category, dietary tag, and free-text query with
  AND semantics, and show a friendly empty state when nothing matches.
- The order form must reject a missing contact method, a pickup date under 48
  hours away, and a quantity below 1; on success it generates a human-readable
  order reference (e.g. GC-2026-0007) and echoes the full order back.
- Prices are shown in GBP with two decimals; totals for quantity > 1 are
  computed.
- All form validation errors are field-level and accessible (associated with the
  input, announced to screen readers).

## Non-functional requirements
- Responsive from 320px to 1440px; mobile-first.
- Core content (menu, hours, contact) readable with JS disabled.
- Semantic HTML landmarks, one h1 per page, alt text on every image.
- Colour contrast at least WCAG AA.
- No third-party trackers.

## Mission
# Golden Crust Bakery — Marketing Website

## What this is
A marketing website for a neighbourhood bakery called Golden Crust. The site is
public, read-mostly, and exists to get a hungry visitor to walk in or place an
order. It must be fast on a phone, work without JavaScript for the core content,
and be trivially editable by the owner.

## Audience
- Local residents deciding where to buy bread and pastries today.
- People ordering a celebration cake or a catering box ahead of time.
- Tourists searching "bakery near me" on a phone.

## Required pages / sections
1. **Home** — hero with today's fresh-bake highlights, opening-hours badge that
   shows Open/Closed computed from the current time and the hours table, and a
   short story block.
2. **Menu** — grouped products (Breads, Pastries, Cakes, Drinks). Each item has a
   name, short description, price, and allergen tags (gluten, dairy, nuts, egg,
   vegan). Filter by dietary tag and by category, plus a text search box.
3. **Hours & Location** — a weekly table of opening hours, a holiday-closures
   list, an embedded static map image, and a "Get directions" link.
4. **Order form** — a celebration-cake / catering enquiry form: name, phone,
   email, pickup date, product, quantity, and free-text notes. Must validate the
   pickup date is at least 48 hours in the future, require either phone or email,
   and show a clear confirmation with an order reference.
5. **Contact** — phone, email, address, social links, and a short FAQ.

## Functional requirements
- Opening-hours logic must be a single source of truth reused by the Home badge
  and the Hours page (compute Open/Closed from the same table).
- The menu filter must combine category, dietary tag, and free-text query with
  AND semantics, and show a friendly empty state when nothing matches.
- The order form must reject a missing contact method, a pickup date under 48
  hours away, and a quantity below 1; on success it generates a human-readable
  order reference (e.g. GC-2026-0007) and echoes the full order back.
- Prices are shown in GBP with two decimals; totals for quantity > 1 are
  computed.
- All form validation errors are field-level and accessible (associated with the
  input, announced to screen readers).

## Non-functional requirements
- Responsive from 320px to 1440px; mobile-first.
- Core content (menu, hours, contact) readable with JS disabled.
- Semantic HTML landmarks, one h1 per page, alt text on every image.
- Colour contrast at least WCAG AA.
- No third-party trackers.

- Online payment / card processing.
- User accounts or login.
- A real database or CMS backend — content is static data in the app.
- Multi-language support.

Submitted form data containing special characters, very long notes, or HTML-like text is echoed back safely without breaking the confirmation.

Pickup date under 48 hours returns a date-specific field-level error stating the minimum allowed date.
Quantity below 1 or non-numeric returns a quantity-specific field-level error.
Missing contact method returns an error on the phone and/or email fields explaining that at least one contact method is required.
A failed or blocked form submission preserves all entered values and displays the field errors without clearing the form or generating an order reference.
A missing hours entry for a day is treated as closed rather than throwing or rendering Open.
An unrecognized allergen tag value or category value on a menu item is ignored for filtering rather than crashing the list.

The confirmation step echoes the full order plus the reference to the user, with no server persistence since no backend exists.

Contact page renders static phone, email, address, social links, and FAQ with alt text on images and no tracker scripts loaded.
